title: Dashboard Capture card fires the OLD exposure while displaying the new one (typed value only commits on Enter)
what_happened: In the Capture dashboard widget I clicked the Exp field, selected all, typed 2, pressed Tab, then pressed Capture. The field kept showing 'Exp: 2' but the native log recorded 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1' and the progress ring read 13% after ~16 s (13% of 120 s = 15.6 s - exact match). Typing the same value and pressing Enter instead did commit (the field renormalised to '3.0' and the capture ran ~3 s). So the card can show one exposure and take a completely different one, indefinitely, with no warning.
expected: Losing focus (Tab, clicking another control, pressing Capture) must commit the edit, or the field must visibly reject/revert the uncommitted text. What the card shows and what it captures must never disagree.
repro: Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Capture Settings -> Done. Click the Exp box, Ctrl+A, type 2, press Tab, press Capture. Watch the progress % and `grep 'Starting.*exposure' /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log`.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-38.png: field reads 'Exp: 2' while the ring reads 13% of a run the log calls 120 s. /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log 18:42:16 'Starting 120s exposure'. Repeated with Tab at a different value (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-41.png: field '2', progress 90% of the previously committed 9 s).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/capture_settings_card.dart:536 - _CompactSettingField wires only `onSubmitted: widget.onChanged`; there is no onEditingComplete/onChanged and no FocusNode listener. didUpdateWidget (:478) only rewrites the controller when the provider value changes, so stale text survives forever. Both Exp and Gain use this field.

title: Tonight card reports a concrete twilight time and 9h28m imaging window while saying 'Location needed'
what_happened: With no observing location set (app_settings.observer_latitude = 0.0, and the command-bar LST reads '--:--:--'), the Tonight dashboard card shows Twilight 15:22, Moon 90%, Window 9h 28m - and in the same card Target: 'Location needed' plus 'Set an observing location to generate target plans.' The twilight/window numbers are computed at latitude 0 / longitude 0 in the machine's local timezone (15:22 local = 19:22 UTC, which is astronomical twilight on the equator on Aug 1), so they are wrong for every real observer, and there is no marking that they are placeholders.
expected: Twilight and Window must render as '--' (like LST and Exposure already do) until a site is set. A user reading 'Window 9h 28m' will plan a session around a number that is not theirs.
repro: Fresh profile, skip onboarding, do not set an observing location. Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Tonight -> Done. Read the Tonight tile.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-34.png (Twilight 15:22, Window 9h 28m, Target 'Location needed'); sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like '%latitude%'" -> observer_latitude|0.0; command bar shows LST '--:--:--' in the same frame.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/tonight_card.dart

title: Polar alignment ends with a green "Alignment Complete" tick and a green "+0%" chip after a 30-arcminute residual error
what_happened: I ran Three-Point Polar Alignment to completion against the simulators (camera+mount connected, ASTAP stub solving). Three points measured, adjust phase entered, then I pressed Done. The result screen shows a large green success check, the headline 'Alignment Complete', 'Final error: 1800.0 arcseconds', and an Alignment Summary reading Before 1800" -> After 1800" with Improvement rendered as a GREEN '+0%' chip. The Alignment History row for the run is likewise stamped with a green checkmark ('Today 10:30 / Final: 1800" / +0%'). 1800 arcsec is 30 arcminutes - half a degree of polar error, 60x the wizard's own Auto-Complete threshold of 30" - and the session improved the alignment by exactly nothing.
expected: The terminal state must be honest about the residual. Success styling (green tick, green chip) belongs only to a run that reached the configured threshold. A run that ends 60x above threshold with 0% improvement should read 'Alignment stopped - still 30' 00" off' in amber/red, and the improvement chip should be neutral or red at <=0%.
repro: Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera + Simulated Mount. Imaging -> Mount tab -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> Start Alignment. Let the 3 points measure, wait for the adjust phase, press Done.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-116.png (green check, 'Alignment Complete', Final error 1800.0 arcseconds, Before 1800" -> After 1800", green +0%). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-118.png (history row, green tick, +0%). DB agrees: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db 'select initial_total_error,final_total_error,auto_completed from polar_alignment_history' -> 1800.00067|1800.00062|0. auto_completed=0 is recorded, so the app KNOWS the threshold was never met, and still renders success.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_screen_parts/ (completion panel + _history_panel.dart row styling)

title: Polar alignment computes and reports azimuth/altitude error at latitude 0, longitude 0 when no observing location is set
what_happened: With no observing location configured (app_settings observer_latitude=0.0, observer_longitude=0.0; Equipment's readiness panel is actively flagging 'No observing location set'), I started TPPA and it ran all three points and produced concrete corrections - 'Azimuth Left 427.6"', 'Altitude Up 2287.9"', final 1800.0". The az/alt decomposition of a polar-axis error is a function of site latitude; at lat 0 the pole sits on the horizon, so every number the wizard printed is the correction for an observer on the equator, not for the user. The native layer has an explicit guard for this (polar_align/mod.rs:390-399 returns 'Polar alignment requires observer latitude/longitude...') but it only fires when the location is None, and the app installs a (0,0) location at startup - app.log: 'Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0' - so the guard can never fire.
expected: Starting polar alignment with no site set must be refused with 'Set your observing location first' (the wizard already refuses on a disconnected camera, a disconnected mount and an unavailable solver), or the site must be part of the pre-flight checklist shown on the idle screen. It must never silently substitute 0,0.
repro: Fresh profile, do not set an observing location. Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera + Mount. Imaging -> Mount tab -> Three-Point Polar Alignment -> Start Alignment. Verify with: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like 'observer_%'" -> observer_latitude|0.0, observer_longitude|0.0.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-115.png (corrections printed), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-116.png (Final error 1800.0 arcseconds), /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log line 80092 'Setting observer location: lat=0, lon=0, elev=0'. Native guard that is bypassed: native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/polar_align/mod.rs:390.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_screen.dart:59-121 (_startAlignment pre-flight has camera/mount/solver checks but no site check); native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/state.rs get_observer_location + the startup path that sets 0,0

title: An aborted polar alignment is written to Alignment History as a success with a green "+97%" improvement badge
what_happened: I started All-Sky polar alignment, let it iterate for ~2 minutes without touching the mount (impossible to touch - it is a simulator), then pressed Stop. The status line correctly read 'Polar alignment stopped'. But a row was still committed to polar_alignment_history and the Alignment History panel now shows 'Today 10:41 / Final: 1376\"' with a green checkmark and a green '+97%' badge. Nothing was adjusted, the user cancelled, and the residual is still 1376\" (23 arcmin). The '97% improvement' is an artefact of the first iteration's noisy 40104\" measurement being taken as 'initial'.
expected: A cancelled run must either not be persisted, or be persisted and displayed as 'Stopped' with a neutral icon and no improvement badge. Improvement must be computed against a stable initial measurement, not the first noisy sample, and must not be reported at all for a run in which the user made no adjustment.
repro: Polar Alignment -> All-Sky -> Start Alignment -> wait ~2 min -> Stop. Scroll the left column to Alignment History. Cross-check: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/data/skotiq.db 'select id,initial_total_error,final_total_error,auto_completed,completed_at from polar_alignment_history' -> row 2: 40104.58|1376.13|0 (auto_completed=0, i.e. threshold never met) yet completed_at is populated.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-132.png (history: 'Today 10:41 Final: 1376\"' green tick, green +97%); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-131.png ('Polar alignment stopped', Total 1376.1\" in red); DB row 2 above.
where: the polar alignment history writer (run finalisation) + packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/polar_alignment_screen_parts/_history_panel.dart row styling

title: Flat Frame Wizard captures at a different camera offset than the Imaging screen (10 vs 50) and never shows which gain/offset it will use
what_happened: At 10:46 the Imaging screen's Camera tab showed 'Gain (0-600) 100 / Offset (0-255) 50', and the app's own light-frame path commands offset 50 (app.log 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50)'). At 10:50 I ran the Flat Frame Wizard on the same camera in the same session, and every one of its seven exposures was commanded as 'gain=Some(100), offset=Some(10)'. The Flat Wizard UI displays no gain or offset anywhere - Quick Capture shows only Filter, Histogram Target, Tolerance and Frame Count - so nothing warns the user. Flats taken at a different offset from the lights carry the wrong bias pedestal and the app's own library matcher refuses them: flat_library_dao.dart:132 states 'gain, offset, and binning must match exactly'.
expected: The flat wizard must capture with the same gain/offset the light frames will use, and it must display them (NINA shows gain/offset/binning on the flat wizard panel and lets you override them). If the two surfaces genuinely have different sources of truth, that is the bug; at minimum the wizard has to show the values it is about to command.
repro: Equipment -> connect Simulated Camera. Imaging -> Camera tab -> read Gain/Offset. Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Start Capture -> choose a folder -> Continue. Then: grep 'gain=Some' /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-136.png (Camera tab: Gain 100, Offset 50). /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log 14:50:34-14:51:03: seven lines 'Starting <t>s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(10), bin=1x1'. Earlier light path in the same profile: 'Starting 120s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/flat_wizard_service.dart:314-323 (offset = profileDefaultOffset ?? currentOffset ?? status.offset) vs the imaging capture path; UI: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/flat_wizard/ (no gain/offset surface)

title: Flat wizard Quick Capture ignores the selected filter and always drives the wheel to position 0
what_happened: With the filter wheel physically at Ha (position 4) I opened the Quick Capture Filter dropdown and chose 'B'. The panel header updated to 'FILTER B'. I pressed Start Capture. The native log shows the app commanded 'api_filterwheel_set_position ... position=0' - i.e. L - and the error banner that followed named the wrong filter too: 'L: filter wheel did not confirm position 0 within 15s'. Same on the previous run: dropdown showed R, the app commanded position=0 and relabelled itself L. The Filter dropdown on Quick Capture is decorative; the run always targets index 0.
expected: Start Capture must move to and expose through the filter the user selected. Flats for the wrong filter are worse than no flats - they will be applied to the wrong channel and corrupt every calibrated frame.
repro: Imaging -> click the Ha chip in the bottom filter row (wheel moves to position 4). Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Filter dropdown -> B (header shows 'FILTER B') -> Start Capture. Then: grep filterwheel_set_position /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log

Earlier repetition with R selected: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-154.png (Filter R) -> app.log 14:57:32 position=0 -> /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-157.png (banner names L).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/flat_wizard/filter_controls.dart (selection) into packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/flat_wizard_provider.dart (the quick-capture run builder, which appears to take the first entry of the filter list rather than the selected one)

title: Flat wizard cannot capture a flat when a filter move is needed - its wheel move neither takes effect nor is confirmed, while the same move works from Equipment
what_happened: Every Quick Capture run that needs a wheel move dies with 'filter wheel did not confirm position 0 within 15s - run stopped.' The native call reports success in the same millisecond - app.log: '[API] api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=0' immediately followed by '[API] Filter wheel position set successfully' - but the Dart filterWheelStateProvider the wizard polls (flat_wizard_provider.dart:1372-1383, waiting for !isMoving && currentPosition == position) never reports the new position, so the wizard fails closed after 15 s. Crucially the wheel itself is fine: issuing the SAME position-0 command from the Equipment screen's filter-wheel card moved it and the card updated to 'L / #1' within ~5 s. So the move works everywhere except from the flat wizard, and after the wizard's two attempts the wheel was still sitting on Ha/#5. The only flat runs that ever reached the exposure stage were the ones where the wheel already happened to be at the target and the move was skipped (line 1346). Zero flats were written across four attempts: /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/flats is empty and flat_history/flat_library have 0 rows.
expected: After a successful filterWheelSetPosition the wheel state must be refreshed (event or poll) so the confirmation loop sees the new position. Failing that, the wizard must say the wheel reported success but never confirmed, and offer to proceed - not just stop.
repro: Connect Simulated Camera + Simulated Filter Wheel. Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Start Capture -> choose a folder -> Continue. Wait 15 s.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-157.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-163.png (the banner); app.log 14:57:32 and 15:01:46 (wizard commands position=0, native reports success, wheel stays on Ha); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-178.png (Equipment card still reading 'Ha / #5' twelve minutes after the wizard's second attempt) vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-181.png (same card reading 'L / #1' five seconds after the Equipment dropdown issued the identical position=0 at 15:14:03); sqlite3 ... 'select count(*) from flat_history' = 0 and 'find /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/flats -type f' returns nothing.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/flat_wizard_provider.dart:1370-1394 (the confirmation loop) and whatever should refresh filterWheelStateProvider after filterWheelSetPosition

title: Co-imaging card says "You are pooling light here" after you explicitly decline to share your subs
what_happened: I connected to a real hub (a locally run skotiq_hub on 127.0.0.1:8091), pressed Start session and created a session on NGC 7000. The app then opened 'Share your co-imaging subs', whose own text says 'Let this rig contribute my completed subs unattended ... Leave unchecked and your subs will NOT be added to the combined stack.' I pressed Cancel, granting nothing. The session card then rendered a green check with 'You are pooling light here'. Nothing is being pooled: no license was accepted, no contribute consent was given, and FRAMES/COMBINED still read 0.
expected: The caption must reflect contribution consent, not mere membership: 'Joined - not contributing (sharing off)' in a neutral colour, with a 'Turn on sharing' action. Telling a user their photons are being pooled when they declined is the most consequential thing this screen can get wrong.
repro: Run a hub: cd server/skotiq_hub && dart run bin/server.dart --port 8091 --bind 127.0.0.1 --db /tmp/ns-audit/hub/hub.db --atlas-root /tmp/ns-audit/hub/atlas --secret 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef. App -> Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate -> Connect to a hub -> http://127.0.0.1:8091 -> Start session (NGC 7000, RA 314.75, Dec 44.31) -> Cancel the sharing dialog.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-175.png (the consent dialog, all three checkboxes unchecked, about to be cancelled) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-176.png (after Cancel: green check 'You are pooling light here', FRAMES 0, COMBINED 0s).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/collaborative_sky/widgets/coimaging_session_card.dart:372-388 - the caption is gated on `joined == true` only, with no reference to the sharing/consent state.

what_happened: Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate -> tapping a collaborative mosaic pushes a full-screen detail page ('M31 Wide Field - Collaborative mosaic - panels split across the club') whose only header controls are the title and a refresh icon. title: Dashboard Mount jog pad fires a 500 ms pulse guide instead of a slew - the arrows do nothing a user can see
what_happened: The Mount Control dashboard widget shows an N/S/E/W arrow pad that looks like a slew/jog pad. Each press calls mountCommandService.pulseGuide(direction), which the native log shows as 'Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east' - about 4 arcseconds at guide rate. RA/Dec on the card stayed at 00:00:00 / +00d00'00" across three presses, no toast, no status change. Press-and-hold for 2 s produced exactly one 500 ms pulse, not a continuous slew.

title: The Smart Night dashboard prompt never appears even with its toggle on and every documented precondition met
what_happened: Settings -> Sequencer -> Smart Night Defaults -> 'Dashboard auto-prompt' ('Show the Smart Night prompt on the dashboard when your equipment is ready') is ON by default and I confirmed the toggle is blue/on. I then satisfied every gate the card checks (smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-127): profile focal length 550 mm and aperture 100 mm saved (equipmentReady), observing location 40.0 / -105.0 and not 0,0, no sequence running, nothing dismissed on a fresh profile, and I waited more than four minutes - well past the 60 s readiness grace. The bottom-centre prompt never appeared, on the briefing dashboard or the cockpit dashboard.
expected: With the toggle on and equipment ready the prompt should slide in from the bottom centre. Either it shows, or the setting should not promise it.
repro: Fresh profile -> Settings -> Location: 40 / -105 -> Equipment -> Edit Profile -> focal length 550, aperture 100 -> connect the four simulators -> Dashboard -> wait 4 minutes.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-212.png (dashboard right after connecting), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-213.png (bottom strip 60 s later), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-214.png (four minutes in - no prompt anywhere); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-217.png and rw-218.png (the 'Dashboard auto-prompt' row and its toggle, on).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-144 - the two remaining suppressors are the 60 s grace rebuild (_equipmentReadyGraceElapsed / _graceTimer) and 'if (draftAsync.isLoading || draftAsync.valueOrNull != null) return SizedBox.shrink()' on pendingSmartNightDraftProvider; a provider that never leaves loading would hide the card forever with no trace.
